summary: None of the four pre-registered scikit-fem configurations can be frozen for E009, so frozen_config.json has feasible: false. The pre-registration was committed as df40ac9 before any solve. The four candidates were Q1 with h0 4 mm / dz_max 1 mm, Q1 with 2 mm / 0.5 mm, Q2 with 4 mm / 5 mm, and Q2 with 4 mm / 2 mm, all with near_margin 2 mm. Q1 misses on accuracy, measured at level 2. q1_h4 is 1.389 K off at the N-layer d3 source mean, against the 0.040 K margin and the 0.05 K of A2. Its A4 on the reference cases is 3.67 K, and the GCI is +inf on both dev layouts because some Tj-max sequences diverge. q1_h2 is 0.680 K off at the N-layer level 2. Q2 is much more accurate (Case 1a at level 2: error 0.0115 K, GCI 0.042 K), but it fails the founder's CG rule. It needs 359 and 352 iterations at level 1 on Case 1a and reaches the 400-iteration cap at level 2 on Cases 1a and 2. Q2 is also still 0.48 K off on the N-layer case at level 1. The gates hold everywhere: energy balance at most 2.4e-11, node-count growth 7.04 to 7.77 per level, every reported point a node on all levels, reference hashes and dev fingerprints verified. The F3 null discriminates: constant k gives a 2.51 K error, failing A1 and A2. 'chosen' in the JSON files is q1_h4. It is listed for the record only, as the cheapest candidate with complete three-level data, and is not a recommendation. That display choice was not pre-specified and is labelled as made after the data. Measured Q2 memory is 3.0 to 6.0 kB per DOF, falling with size. The E009 tables per candidate range from a 4.7 GB peak and 0.4 h (q1_h4) to 18.3 GB and 3.7 h (q2_h4z2). All fit the n2-highmem-32 burst VM. The local run stayed under 5.64 GB peak, one solve at a time. Separately, I found and fixed a flaw in my own instrumentation. pyamg's preconditioner calls the same solve object, so my first counter recorded 2n+1 instead of n CG iterations. Old entries were converted by (n-1)/2, and a re-solve confirmed it: 154 predicted, 154 counted, bit-identical residual. Commands and exit codes: the --plan run exited 0. The first study launch exited 1 on a cache bookkeeping bug (no solve affected); after the fix the study exited 0. --report exited 0, ruff exited 0, both DoD python checks exited 0, and `mfos gate --fast` reported 'all gates passed'.
root_cause: Two measured obstacles. (1) The N-layer DBC reference case is badly under-resolved. Its die-sized flux patches sit on thin layers (0.18 mm die, 0.05 mm attach, 0.3 mm Cu, 0.38 mm ceramic). The source-mean error converges slowly, at observed order about 1.2 for Q1, so reaching 0.05 K needs lateral cells near the source edges far below what h0 with near_margin's x1/x2/x4 steps gives. Refining by r = 2 in x, y and z over three levels then puts the 300 mm Muzychka plates at tens of millions of DOF. (2) Q2's AMG-CG uses up its iteration headroom on the weak-Robin 10 mm plates (Cases 1a and 2): over 300 iterations at level 1 and the 400 cap at level 2. Neither is an implementation defect in the configurations tested. The objective's A2/K2 pair, the r = 2 three-level rule, and the affordable grid budget do not fit together for the N-layer case with this grid rule.
evidence: [F] q1_h4 level 2: N-layer d3 source mean 402.03 / 408.92 / 411.86 K vs reference 413.25 K (|err| 1.389 K, GCI 3.67 K, observed order about 1.2); dev_study.json candidates.q1_h4.cases.nlayer_dbc
[F] q1_h2 level 2: N-layer max |err| 0.680 K, GCI 2.00 K; side_by_side_6 has 8 divergent Tj-max sequences
[F] q2_h4: Case 1a level 2 |err| 0.0115 K, GCI 0.042 K; CG max iterations by level on Case 1a 249 / 359 / 400 (cap); on Case 2 190 / 288 / 400; N-layer level 1 |err| 0.482 K
[F] q2_h4z2: CG 352 on Case 1a level 1, 400 on Case 2 level 2
[F] Case 1b, Case 3 and the manufactured case meet A1, A2 and A4 for every candidate (worst manufactured-case error 0.0085 K for Q1)

[F] Gates: energy balance at most 2.4e-11; manufactured Q_out within 1e-6 of 64.648 W; Picard below 1e-4 K; node-count growth 7.04 to 7.77, inside 8 +/- 15 %; reported points are nodes at identical coordinates on all levels

[F] Reference hashes befc5efa (series) and ca05847b (manufactured) verified; dev fingerprints 1f66b68a and 6aaf383a equal E006.yaml; only dev seed 20261101 used

alternative_explanations.explanation: The frozen N-layer reference value of the source mean is wrong, or it means something other than the solver's Galerkin face mean.
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Three facts argue against it: the error moves monotonically toward the reference under refinement for both Q1 and Q2; Cases 1b and 3 and the manufactured case agree to 0.0003-0.008 K through the same code; and the series' own convergence is gated in E006. A direct test would be one Q2 level-2 N-layer solve on the burst VM (3.06 M DOF, about 12-14 GB): an error that stalls near a nonzero value would point to the reference.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The large CG counts come from slivers created by the reference-maximum mandatory lines, not from the weak Robin coupling.
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Re-run Case 1a and Case 2 at level 1 without the maximum lines (centroid lines only) and compare the iteration counts. Not run here, to stay within the brief (no solver changes) and the budget.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Q1 divergent or oscillatory Tj-max sequences on the layouts are caused by the argmax node moving between levels, not by a lack of grid convergence.
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Compare the Tj value at a fixed node that persists across levels with Tj max. The argmax node already moves on 14 of 16 dies (recorded per level in dev_study.json).

discriminating_tests: Done: re-solve with the corrected CG counter (predicted 154, counted 154, identical residual)
Done: monotone convergence of every failing point toward its reference, with GCI bracketing the true error (q1_h4 N-layer: GCI 3.67 K against an error of 1.39 K)
Not run (needs the burst VM): Q2 level 2 on the N-layer case, to confirm the extrapolated error of about 0.1 K
Not run: Case 1a and Case 2 level-1 CG counts without the maximum mandatory lines, to separate sliver effects from weak-Robin conditioning
recommended_actions: Founder decision before E009 is designed: no pre-registered configuration reaches A2 (0.05 K) on the N-layer source means at an affordable three-level, r = 2 grid. With any of the four, E009 would trip K2 (> 0.25 K) through a discretisation shortfall, not a model error. Options, each needing a new pre-registered study: (a) a builder task adding edge grading toward the sources to the thermal_fem grid rule; (b) Q2 with a finer h0 near sources only, costed on the burst VM; (c) revisit the resolution budget or criteria for the N-layer case at objective level.

Implementation task, with its own review: AMG-CG headroom for Q2 on the weak-Robin plates. It reaches the 400 cap at level 2 on Cases 1a and 2, and those solves pass only through the 1e-8 final check. Options include the preconditioner, the cap, or the snap policy. Until then Q2 is ineligible under the T0218 rule.
Keep the corrected CG instrumentation (count only the outer accel='cg' call) in the E009 runner. pyamg's residuals list and a naive callback both miscount.

Optional founder dev burst to complete the missing levels (the verdict does not depend on it): scripts/burst_gcp.sh --cmd "uv run python research/scripts/o007_dev_study.py --full" research/o007_dev (it resumes from the cache).
